content: Folliculitis refers to the inflammation of one or more hair follicles. This condition can develop on any part of the skin. Symptoms of Folliculitis The common symptoms of folliculitis include the appearance of a rash, itching, and the development of pimples or pustules near hair follicles. These are often observed in areas such as the neck, groin, or genital region. The pimples may eventually form a crust. Causes of Folliculitis Folliculitis typically begins when hair follicles are damaged. This damage can result from friction caused by clothing, blockage of the follicle, or shaving. Once the follicles are damaged, they are often infected by the bacterium Staphylococcus aureus (commonly referred to as staph). A specific type of folliculitis, known as barber's itch, is a staph infection that affects the hair follicles in the beard area, particularly on the upper lip. Shaving tends to exacerbate this condition. Another similar condition, called tinea barbae, is caused by a fungal infection rather than bacteria. High-Risk Groups Pseudofolliculitis barbae is a condition that predominantly affects Black men. It occurs when curly beard hairs are cut too short, causing them to curve back into the skin, leading to inflammation. Diagnosis The diagnosis of folliculitis is primarily based on the appearance of the skin. Laboratory tests may be conducted to identify the specific bacteria or fungus responsible for the infection. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care If symptoms of folliculitis recur frequently, persist for more than 2 to 3 days, or if the infection begins to spread, it is important to apply home treatments and contact a healthcare provider. Treatment Options Applying hot, moist compresses can help promote drainage of the affected follicles. Treatment may involve the use of topical antibiotics, such as mupirocin, or oral antibiotics, such as dicloxacillin. In cases of fungal infections, antifungal medications may be prescribed to control the infection. Medical Care for Folliculitis Patients can seek treatment for folliculitis at hospitals or clinics that specialize in dermatological conditions. Prognosis Folliculitis generally responds well to treatment. However, it is possible for the condition to recur.
